title: Psychiatrist Salary Australia: Award Rates, Hourly Conversion, and Take-Home Pay
description: Understand psychiatrist salary Australia with award rates from Fair Work, hourly to annual conversion at 38 hours, tax, super, and casual loading explained.
salarySummary: Psychiatrists in Australia are covered by the Medical Practitioners Award, with minimum rates set by classification; for a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the annual gross salary is hourly rate × 38 × 52.

faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for a psychiatrist under the Medical Practitioners Award?
faqs.a: The Medical Practitioners Award [MA000031] sets minimum rates for psychiatrists based on classification and experience. For example, a Level 1 medical practitioner (intern) has a minimum hourly rate of $35.19 (AQF Level 8, 1st year) as per the Health Professionals and Support Services Award for comparison, but psychiatrists fall under a separate award. You can find the exact rates in the Fair Work Ombudsman's pay guides for the Medical Practitioners Award.

faqs.q: How do I convert a psychiatrist's hourly rate to annual salary?
faqs.a: Use the formula: hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For a full-time psychiatrist working 38 ordinary hours per week, annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52. If the rate already includes casual loading (25% on top of the minimum hourly rate), ensure you use the base rate before loading for the calculation. The [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool on this site can help.

faqs.q: What is the casual loading for psychiatrists and how does it affect pay?
faqs.a: Casual employees under the Health Professionals and Support Services Award receive a 25% loading on the minimum hourly rate in lieu of entitlements like paid leave. For psychiatrists covered by the Medical Practitioners Award, casual loading may also apply. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how to calculate it. Remember, super is paid on top of the loaded rate.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Psychiatrist Salary Australia

When researching **psychiatrist salary Australia**, it's important to distinguish between award minimum rates, market averages, and the National Minimum Wage. Psychiatrists are medical specialists, and their employment is typically governed by the **Medical Practitioners Award 2020** [MA000031], as referenced by the Fair Work Ombudsman. This award sets minimum hourly rates for different classifications and experience levels.

### Award Rates vs National Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38‑hour week. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. However, psychiatrists earn well above these minimums. The **Medical Practitioners Award** provides specific rates; for example, a Level 1 medical practitioner (intern) at AQF Level 8, 1st year, has a minimum hourly rate of $35.19 (based on the Health Professionals and Support Services Award for comparable roles). More experienced psychiatrists fall into higher classifications, such as Level 2 or above, with rates exceeding $50 per hour.

### Hourly to Annual Conversion

To convert an hourly rate to an annual salary, use the standard formula:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full‑time employee working 38 ordinary hours per week (as defined in the award), the calculation is:

Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52

For example, if a psychiatrist earns $60 per hour, the annual gross is $60 × 38 × 52 = $118,560. This assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, and no penalty rates. The [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool on this site automates this calculation.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find the gross fortnightly amount, multiply the weekly pay by 2. Using the same example, weekly pay at 38 hours is $60 × 38 = $2,280, so fortnightly gross is $4,560.

### Tax and Superannuation

From the annual gross, you can estimate tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds).

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (the super guarantee rate from 1 July 2026), up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a $118,560 salary, the employer would contribute $14,227.20 per year in super. This is not deducted from your pay; it's an additional benefit. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more details.

### Casual Loading

If you work as a casual psychiatrist, you are entitled to a 25% loading on the minimum hourly rate (or on the agreed rate if higher). This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave and other entitlements. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how to apply it. Do not include the loading in the base rate you enter into the timesheet; instead, use the checkbox to add it automatically.

### Average Earnings for Psychiatrists

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) provides data on earnings, but for psychiatrists, the median full‑time weekly earnings are not published due to high standard error, as noted by Jobs and Skills Australia. However, the average full‑time hours worked per week for psychiatrists is 44 hours, which is above the standard 38 hours. This means many psychiatrists work overtime, which should be paid at penalty rates under the award.

### Using the Timesheet

The [timesheet](/) on this site lets you enter your base hourly rate (without casual loading) and choose whether to add the 25% loading. It then calculates your weekly, fortnightly, monthly, and annual gross pay, along with estimated tax and super. Remember, the results are estimates and do not account for overtime, allowances, or salary sacrifice.

### Key Takeaways

- **Psychiatrist salary Australia** is governed by the Medical Practitioners Award, with minimum rates well above the National Minimum Wage.
- Use the formula hourly × 38 × 52 for a full‑time annual salary.
- Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum rate.
- Super is paid at 12% on top of ordinary earnings, up to the contribution cap.
- Tax is progressive with the Medicare levy.

For more detailed award rates, refer to the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman. You can also explore [reference tables](/data) for historical rates and [average pay](/topics/average-pay) for other occupations.
